newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Shell confirms Australia oil discovery.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Shell confirms Australia oil discovery.

text.p: Shell Australia Ltd confirmed on Friday that a joint-venture exploration team had made an oil and gas find in the Browse Basin offshore northwest Australia.

"We believe this oil and gas accumulation could be comparable in size to other recent discoveries in the Greater North West Shelf on the initial information we possess," Shell Australia chairman Roland Williams said in a statement.

The find was made in permit WA-241-P, held by Royal Dutch/Shell unit Shell Development (Australia) Pty Ltd with 50 percent and Cultus Petroleum NL and Chevron Corp unit, Chevron Asiatic Ltd, with 25 percent each.

Shell's announcement came after Cultus told the Australian Stock Exchange (ASX) on Friday that results of drill stem tests of the Cornea 1 and 1b wells in WA-241-P were "positive with respect to an oil/gas discovery".
It said Cornea 2, spudded last Sunday, is now running wireline logs after reaching total depth of 880 metres.
Cultus shares soared on the news, ending at A$1.90, up 45 cents on Thursday's close.
Cultus had previously secured an ASX waiver allowing it not to issue regular drilling reports about the Cornea wells because disclosure might affect applications for nearby areas.
The Western Australian state government welcomed the news and held out hopes that the discovery could herald a new province.

"The fact that oil has been discovered raises hopes that more oil and gas will be discovered in the basin, which currently has seven permits," state Resources Development Minister Colin Barnett said in a statement.

"If subsequent testing proves up its siginificance, I would hope this discovery foreshadows the development of what would be the second significant oil and gas industry development off the Western Australian coast, alongside the Carnarvon Basin...."
